chunks: And Al-A'la narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to me: 'When a man lies on his right side, let him say: In the name of Allah, O Allah, I have submitted my self to You, and turned my face to You, and entrusted my affair to You, and leaned my back upon You, I have placed my trust in You, out of fear of You and hope in You. There is no refuge and no deliverance from You except to You. I have believed in Your Book which You revealed and in Your Messenger whom You sent.
Then let him recite the Tasbih of Fatimah al-Zahra (peace be upon her).
And whoever is struck by fear when he goes to sleep, let him recite when he lies down on his bed - the two Surahs of protection (Al-Falaq and An-Nas) and the Verse of the Throne (Ayat al-Kursi).

key_terms.آيَةَ الْكُرْسِيِّ: The Verse of the Throne (Ayat al-Kursi, Quran 2:255)
key_terms.الْمُعَوِّذَتَيْنِ: The two Surahs of protection (Al-Falaq and An-Nas)
key_terms.تَسْبِيحَ فَاطِمَةَ: The specific set of glorifications attributed to Fatimah al-Zahra (AS)
key_terms.تَوَسَّدَ: To lie down with the head resting on the hand/side

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended prayers and verses to recite before sleeping in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Transmitted in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS) prescribes a comprehensive bedtime ritual that integrates personal submission (tawakkul) with the renowned Tasbih of Fatimah al-Zahra (SA), emphasizing the continuity of prophetic tradition. It further instructs reciting the Mu'awwidhat and Ayat al-Kursi to ward off nocturnal fears, reflecting the Shia emphasis on spiritual protection through Quranic verses and the intercessory legacy of the Ahl al-Bayt.
